title: Level 5 (World Class) - B-6
notes:
West leads the ♠J against 6♥. West has shown at least 5 diamonds and 5 clubs with his unusual no trump. West is very likely to have the ♦K. If his spade lead is a singleton, the contract has no chance. South should assume that West started with a doubleton ♠J10 (and thus no more than a singleton heart).

East wins the ♠A (ducking is superior) and South should drop the ♠K. East continues the suit and North wins the ♠Q.

South can now set up 2 spade winners by taking a ruffing finesse against the ♠9. This play will not work while West has a trump as East will not cover. South must plan to draw West's singleton trump while keeping the lead in the dummy. It will also be necessary to keep a late dummy entry in trumps to enjoy the long spades. South's best play is to finesse against the ♥10 in East's hand.

The ♥8 or ♥9 is played and when East follows low, so does South. When West produces a low heart, spades can safely be played. When East covers with the ♠9, South ruffs. East's remaining trumps can be drawn ending in the dummy. North will have 2 established spades for South's diamond losers.
